core.m1: A security check is an airport safety inspection.
core.m2: Passengers and bags are checked before entering the boarding area.
core.e1: The security check is on the second floor.
core.e2: Please arrive early for the security check.
core.p1: The _______ is on the second floor.

core.m1: An X-ray machine looks inside bags.
core.m2: It helps officers find restricted items.
core.e1: Put your backpack in the X-ray machine.
core.e2: The X-ray machine checks every carry-on bag.

core.m1: A metal detector finds metal on your body.
core.m2: You walk through it during airport security.
core.e1: Walk slowly through the metal detector.
core.e2: My belt made the metal detector beep.

core.m1: A liquid is something that can flow, such as water.
core.m2: Airport rules limit liquids in carry-on bags.
core.e2: Put small liquids in a clear bag.
core.p2: Put small _______ in a clear bag.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="15" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="11" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: Remove means to take something away or off.
core.m2: At security, you may remove a jacket or laptop.
core.e2: I need to remove my laptop from the bag.
core.p2: I need to _______ my laptop from the bag.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="16" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="8" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: A security officer checks passengers and bags.
core.m2: The officer gives instructions at the security checkpoint.
core.e1: The security officer asked me to open my bag.
core.e2: Please listen to the security officer.
core.p1: The _______ asked me to open my bag.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="12" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="9" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: Immigration is the border check when you enter a country.
core.m2: An officer asks about your trip and documents.
core.e1: We go to immigration after landing.
core.e2: The immigration line is very long.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="13" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="10" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: A visa is permission to enter or stay in a country.
core.m2: Some travelers need one before their trip.
core.e1: My visa is in my passport.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="14" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="11" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: An entry stamp is a mark placed in a passport.
core.m2: It can show when you entered a country.
core.e1: The officer gave me an entry stamp.
core.e2: My entry stamp shows today's date.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="15" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="8" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: Customs checks goods that enter a country.
core.m2: You may need to report food, gifts, or expensive items.
core.e1: We went through customs after immigration.
core.e2: The customs officer asked about my food.
core.p2: The _______ officer asked about my food.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="16" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="9" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: Declare means to officially report an item.
core.m2: Travelers declare goods when the rules require it.
core.e1: I need to declare this food.
core.e2: Do I have to declare these gifts?
core.p2: Do I have to _______ these gifts?

core.m1: Passport control is where an officer checks your passport.
core.m2: It is part of entering or leaving a country.
core.e2: We waited twenty minutes at passport control.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="13" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="11" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: The boarding area is where passengers wait for a flight.
core.m2: It is usually near the departure gate.
core.e1: Our boarding area is beside Gate 12.
core.e2: Food is available near the boarding area.
core.svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 80 80"><rect x="14" y="18" width="52" height="44" rx="9" fill="none" stroke="#1B2A4A" stroke-width="2"/><circle cx="40" cy="40" r="8" fill="#C8956C"/></svg>

core.m1: A connecting flight is the next flight in a multi-flight trip.
core.m2: You change planes before reaching your final destination.
core.e1: My connecting flight leaves in one hour.
core.e2: Where do I go for my connecting flight?
core.p2: Where do I go for my _______?

core.m1: Line up means to stand in a queue.
core.m2: Passengers line up before security and boarding.
core.e1: Please line up behind the blue sign.
core.e2: We need to line up for passport control.
core.p2: We need to _______ for passport control.

extended.m: A pat-down is a manual check by a security officer.
extended.ex: The officer gave me a quick pat-down.

extended.m: A laptop is a portable computer.
extended.ex: Please take your laptop out of the bag.

extended.m: A restricted item is something not allowed through security.
extended.ex: Scissors are a restricted item in carry-on bags.

extended.m: A sharp object can cut or injure someone.
extended.ex: Pack sharp objects in your checked luggage.

extended.m: A random check is an unplanned extra inspection.
extended.ex: I was chosen for a random check today.

extended.m: A body scanner checks passengers without touching them.
extended.ex: Step into the body scanner, please.

extended.m: A tray holds your items as they go through the X-ray machine.
extended.ex: Put your phone and keys in the tray.

extended.m: A conveyor belt moves bags through the X-ray machine.
extended.ex: Watch your bag move along the conveyor belt.

extended.m: An ID check confirms who you are.
extended.ex: There is an ID check before the gate.

extended.m: Duty-free means no local tax is charged on the item.
extended.ex: I bought perfume at the duty-free shop.

extended.m: The seat belt sign tells passengers to stay seated.
extended.ex: The seat belt sign turned on during landing.

extended.m: A safety demonstration shows what to do in an emergency.
extended.ex: Please watch the safety demonstration before takeoff.

extended.m: An overhead bin stores bags above your seat.
extended.ex: There is no space left in the overhead bin.

extended.m: Standby means waiting for a seat that may become available.
extended.ex: I am on standby for the next flight.

extended.m: A fingerprint is the unique pattern on your finger.
extended.ex: The officer scanned my fingerprint at the counter.

extended.m: A biometric photo records your face for identity checks.
extended.ex: The kiosk took a biometric photo of me.

extended.m: An entry requirement is something you must have to enter a country.
extended.ex: A valid visa is an entry requirement here.

extended.m: Length of stay means how long you plan to remain.
extended.ex: My length of stay is ten days.

extended.m: Purpose of visit means the reason for your trip.
extended.ex: My purpose of visit is a family wedding.

extended.m: An arrival card is a form filled out on entry.
extended.ex: Please complete the arrival card before landing.

extended.m: An immigration officer checks passports and travel documents.
extended.ex: The immigration officer asked how long I would stay.

extended.m: A customs form lists items you are bringing into a country.
extended.ex: I filled out the customs form on the plane.

extended.m: Nothing to declare means you have no restricted or taxable items.
extended.ex: I chose the nothing to declare lane.

extended.m: A transit passenger stops at an airport without leaving it.
extended.ex: Transit passengers can wait in the lounge.

extended.m: A layover is a stop between two flights.
extended.ex: I have a two-hour layover in Tokyo.

extended.m: A gate change means your departure gate has been switched.
extended.ex: There was a last-minute gate change to B14.

extended.m: A final call is the last announcement before boarding closes.
extended.ex: This is the final call for Flight 582.

extended.m: A boarding group is the order in which passengers board.
extended.ex: My boarding group is called first.

extended.m: Priority boarding lets certain passengers board early.
extended.ex: Priority boarding starts in five minutes.

extended.m: A boarding pass shows your flight, seat, and gate.
extended.ex: Please have your boarding pass ready.

phrases.en: Do I need to remove my shoes?
phrases.note: Ask this before you walk through the metal detector.

phrases.zh: 我沒有需要申報的物品。
phrases.note: Use this at customs if you are not carrying restricted items.
A common answer at passport control about your purpose of visit.

phrases.en: Where do I go for my connecting flight?
phrases.zh: 我要去哪裡搭轉機航班？
phrases.note: Ask airport staff for directions after landing.

phrases.en: Could you please repeat the question?
phrases.zh: 可以請您再說一次問題嗎？
phrases.note: Use this politely if you do not understand an officer.

dialogues.title: At the Security Check
dialogues.sit: You are preparing your bags for airport security.
lines: Excuse me, do I need to remove my shoes?
No, but please remove your jacket.
Should I take out my laptop?
Yes. Put it in a separate tray.
That is fine. Please place it in the clear bag.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask whether you need to remove your belt.
dialogues.tn: Focus on polite security questions with Do I need to...?

dialogues.title: At Passport Control
dialogues.sit: You arrive at passport control after landing.
lines: May I see your passport, please?
What is the purpose of your visit?
I will stay for ten days.
dialogues.tp: Try again: say you are visiting friends for one week.
dialogues.tn: Practice short factual answers about purpose and length of stay.

dialogues.title: A Liquid Problem
dialogues.sit: Your carry-on bag has a liquid that is too large.
lines: This bottle is too large for your carry-on bag.
Oh, I did not know. Can I keep it?
You cannot take it through security.
You can throw it away or return to check it in.
I understand. I will throw it away.
Thank you. Please continue to the metal detector.
Okay. Thank you for your help.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask if you can put the bottle in checked luggage.
dialogues.tn: Problem scenario: stay calm and ask about your options.

dialogues.title: At Customs
dialogues.sit: You are asked questions after collecting your luggage.
lines: Yes, I have some packaged snacks.
Did you declare them on your form?
Thank you. Please show them to me.
Of course. They are in this bag.
Everything is fine. You may continue.
dialogues.tp: Try again: say that you have no food and nothing to declare.
dialogues.tn: Practice honest, calm answers about declared items.

dialogues.title: Finding a Connecting Flight
dialogues.sit: You need directions to your connecting flight.
lines: Excuse me, where do I go for my connecting flight?
Please follow the purple signs to Terminal B.
Do I need to pass security again?
Yes. The security check is before Gate B12.
Thank you. Is it far from here?
It is about a ten-minute walk.
dialogues.tp: Try again: ask about a gate change and the boarding time.
dialogues.tn: Ask for directions using Where do I go for...?

speaking.q: What do you put in a security tray?
speaking.h: I put my phone, keys, and laptop in the tray.

speaking.q: Do you usually travel with liquids?
speaking.h: Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

speaking.q: What questions can an immigration officer ask?
speaking.h: An officer can ask about your purpose of visit and length of stay.

speaking.q: What should you do if you do not understand an officer?
speaking.h: Use: Could you please repeat the question?

speaking.q: Describe each step from airport security to your connecting gate.
speaking.h: First I go through security, then...

culture.title: Clear and Honest Border Answers
culture.tz: 清楚且誠實地回答入境問題
culture.photo: 📷 An illustrated immigration officer asking a traveler simple questions at a counter.
culture.notes: Border officers often ask short, direct questions. Travelers should answer truthfully, use simple language, and show the requested documents. This is communication practice, not legal or immigration advice.
qs: What documents do travelers usually prepare?
How can you ask an officer to repeat a question?
Why are short and truthful answers important?

culture.title: Security Procedures Can Vary
culture.tz: 各機場安檢流程可能不同
culture.photo: 📷 An illustrated airport security line with signs guiding passengers through different steps.
culture.notes: The exact procedure may change by airport, country, or current security rules. Watch the signs and follow the officer's instructions instead of assuming every airport is the same.
qs: Which items do travelers often place in a tray?
What should you do when a rule is unclear?
How can arriving early reduce stress?
